diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State $\mathcal{R}_z \gets$ compute cyclotomic factorization of the ratio via Eq.~\eqref{eq:ratio_Rz}

issues.failure_explanation: For the stated 6j summand t_z = (-1)^z [z+1]!/(prod_i [z-a_i]! prod_y [b_y-z]!), the consecutive ratio is uniquely R_z = t_{z+1}/t_z = -[z+2]_q prod_y [b_y-z]_q / prod_i [z+1-a_i]_q: the a-factors belong in the denominator and the b-factors (with argument b_y-z, not b_y-z-1) in the numerator. The printed equation swaps numerator and denominator and shifts the b-argument by one. Concretely, for {1,1,1;1,1,1} (a_i=3, b_y=4, z=3..4) the true ratio at z=3 is -5, while the printed formula has [b_y-z-1]_q = [0]_q = 0 in the denominator (a pole); in general at z = z_max-1 the minimizing y gives [b_y-z_max]_q = 0, so the printed final ratio diverges even though the true sum terminates. Algorithm 1 and the DCR definition both compute the ratio sequence via this equation, so the constructed DCR does not represent the stated 6j series.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed ratio by the uniquely forced correct one, R_z = -[z+2]_q prod_{y=1}^3 [b_y-z]_q / prod_{i=1}^4 [z+1-a_i]_q; no further changes are required anywhere else in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The ratio sequence produced by Algorithm 1 and stored in the DCR tuple (Definition DCR, 'computed via Eq. (eq:ratio_Rz)') is wrong for the 6j-symbol, so the compiled object encodes a different amplitude and the identity S(q) = Pi_q(S_DCR) of prop:deformation_as_evaluation fails for the constructed object. Complexity and stability claims are structurally unaffected because the corrected ratio has the same factor count (K = 8).
issues.title: Hypergeometric update ratio Eq. (eq:ratio_Rz) is inverted and mis-shifted relative to the stated 6j summand
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single, forced, local correction of one displayed formula (not a pure typo, since the central construction consumes the erroneous formula and several tokens are simultaneously wrong, but the correction is unique and routine); the corrected ratio has identical structure and factor count, so every substantive claim, rate, and guarantee survives with no new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For symbolic evaluation, one may take $\mathbb{T} = \Q(\zeta_{2h})$, the cyclotomic number field generated by a primitive root $\zeta_{2h}$.
The entire square root is resolved at the exponent level, without field extension and without any polynomial computation.

issues.failure_explanation: The even/odd exponent split only defers the square root to evaluation: the algorithm returns sqrt(Pi_T(M_rad)) times elements of T. Generically Pi_T(M_rad) is not a square in the exact field, so the postcondition 'Evaluated amplitude S in T' fails and exact evaluation cannot stay in Q(zeta_{2h}). Concrete counterexample: the admissible level-3 Racah 6j-symbol {1/2,1/2,0;3/2,3/2,1}_q at q = exp(i pi/5) equals -phi^{-1/2} with phi = 2 cos(pi/5) (prefactor phi^{-3/2} times sum -phi); Q(sqrt(phi)) is a non-Galois quartic extension of Q, hence by Kronecker-Weber is contained in no cyclotomic field at all, a fortiori not in Q(zeta_{10}). The classical value sqrt(21)/30 of {1,2,2;2,1,2} shows the same phenomenon at q -> 1. Thus the claim that the square root is handled 'without field extension' is true only at compilation time, the exact-projection regime T = Q(zeta_{2h}) cannot deliver generic 6j amplitudes, and the abstract/Fig. 1 claim that evaluation in 'any target field' is realized as a ring homomorphism fails where the square root does not exist; additionally the branch of the square root for real/complex targets is never specified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the 'without field extension' claim to the compilation stage; define exact projection into the (generally non-cyclotomic) quadratic extension T(sqrt(Pi_T(M_rad))) or return the exact pair (Pi(M_root) S_sum, Pi(M_rad)); and fix a square-root branch for numerical targets. Complexity and memory scaling survive unchanged up to the constant-factor field-degree doubling.
issues.overall_effect: The exact algebraic projection regime (Sec. 4, regime 2), the square-root capability claim attached to eq:sqrt_decomp, the 'any target field' framing (abstract and Fig. fig:dcr_architecture), and Algorithm 2's input-output contract are unreliable whenever the square-free part projects to a non-square in T, which is the generic situation for recoupling prefactors.
issues.title: Final square root in DCR projection is not defined in the declared exact target field; 'without field extension' claim fails in general
issues.why_classification: The repair withdraws an advertised capability (exact evaluation in Q(zeta_{2h}) without any field extension) for a whole projection regime and requires a contained but genuine modification of the algorithm's output contract and of several claims; it needs no new global architecture and leaves recognizably comparable results, so it is more than minor but not serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This produces a dense table in $\mathcal{O}(D \log D)$ time
\mathcal{O}\!\left( D_{\max} \cdot C_{\mathbb{T}} + Z \cdot K \cdot S_{\max} \cdot C_{\mathbb{T}} \right), \q

issues.failure_explanation: Compiling the cyclotomic factorization of all quantum integers [m]_q for m <= D_max requires the divisor-incidence data {(m,d): d | m, d > 1}, whose total size is sum_{m <= D} tau(m) = D log D + O(D) by Dirichlet's divisor-sum asymptotic. Generating this data by a sieve costs Theta(D log D) integer operations and storage, and factoring each m on demand costs more; O(D_max) total precomputation is therefore not attainable, and the theorem's bound should read O(D_max log D_max + Z K S_max). The same undercount appears in the first term of prop:added-1 and contradicts the paper's own statement that the complex-analytic cyclotomic table costs O(D log D).

failure_location.quote: Precomputation of cyclotomic data up to $D_{\max}$ contributes $\mathcal{O}(D_{\max})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the precomputation term by O(D_max log D_max) in both bounds (or state explicitly that divisor/cyclotomic incidence data is assumed precomputed and excluded from the operation count).
issues.overall_effect: The stated construction complexity (thm:added-1) and evaluation complexity (prop:added-1) are each off by a factor log D_max in their precomputation terms; the 'near-linear in Z' conclusion, the linear memory scaling, and all benchmarks are unaffected.
issues.title: Precomputation cost in the construction/evaluation complexity bounds is undercounted by a logarithmic factor
issues.why_classification: A short, local correction of the big-O terms with a standard divisor-sum estimate; the method, the near-linear conclusions, the rates in Z, and the advertised scope all survive, with no new lemma or replacement argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider the Turaev-Viro partition function over a triangulated $3$-manifold $\mathcal{M}$, which requires a coherent summation over all admissible spin colorings $\{j\}$:
the Biedenharn-Elliott pentagon identity, which ensures the triangulation independence of topological invariants

issues.failure_explanation: The Turaev-Viro invariant expressed through Racah-Wigner 6j-symbols (the symbol defined in eq:racah_6j) requires, besides the tetrahedral 6j factors and the vertex normalization, the edge weights given by quantum dimensions (prod_e w_{j_e}^2, w_j^2 = [2j+1]_q). Without these factors the right-hand side is not invariant under the Pachner moves - the 1-4/0-2 moves and the orthogonality (bubble) relation produce precisely the quantum-dimension factors - so the displayed expression depends on the triangulation and does not define TV_k(M).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the standard quantum-dimension edge weights (and the corresponding normalization) into the displayed formula.
issues.overall_effect: Only the illustrative macroscopic discussion of Sec. 6.3 is affected; no formal DCR result, algorithm, or benchmark depends on the exact form of eq:TV.
issues.title: Displayed Turaev-Viro state sum omits the quantum-dimension edge weights, so it is not the TV invariant
issues.why_classification: A local correction to an illustrative displayed definition with no downstream dependence; every substantive claim of the paper survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the DCR architecture removes repeated algebraic recomputation, isolating the exponential cost inherent in topological state sums.
Because the combinatorial construction and the numerical evaluation are fused, exact computations are hard \cite{Jaeger1990}.
This separation of structure and evaluation renders large-scale topological state sums computationally tractable.

issues.failure_explanation: What the paper establishes is amortization: each geometrically distinct 6j weight is compiled once and reused, reducing redundant algebraic work, while the paper itself acknowledges that the global sum over colorings retains 'the exponential cost inherent in topological state sums' and cites the hardness of exact TV computation. The claim that the DCR 'renders such large-scale computations tractable' (Sec. 6.3) and 'renders large-scale topological state sums computationally tractable' (conclusion) asserts a tractability guarantee for an exponential-time problem that the formal content does not support; the established gain is a (possibly large) constant-factor/amortization improvement, not a change in the asymptotic complexity of state sums.

failure_location.quote: By severing the compilation of the local geometric weights from the global topological summation, the DCR renders such large-scale computations tractable.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the two sentences to state that the DCR removes redundant recomputation of local weights and amortizes their compilation, while the exponential global summation is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Only the advertised application scope for Turaev-Viro/spin-foam state sums is misleading; no theorem, algorithm, or benchmark is affected.
issues.title: Prose overclaim that the DCR 'renders large-scale topological state sums computationally tractable'
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local qualification of two prose sentences; all technical content, rates, and guarantees survive, and the only loss is an unsupported scope assertion.
